Admins now have more control over how AI credits are used in their teams and organizations. Admins can set a "Custom credit limit" for individual users to control how many AI credits any one person can use. When users hit the limit, they can send a request to their admin to raise their limit.
Learn more in the help center

Organize files the way your team actually works with nested folders. Folders replace Projects and can be nested and colorized to add structure that can flex as your work grows.
Projects are now folders. All files in Teams now live in folders. All previous references to Projects in the UI have been renamed to Folders.
Folder nesting and colors. Nest folders up to 10 layers deep and assign folders colors to create hierarchy.
Simpler sharing. Nested folders inherit access from the folder above it, or you can limit access to specific people.
Folders are rolling out over the coming weeks to all users on all plans.
Learn more in the help center
From treating code as a proposal to turning handoffs into conversations,
read the story of how nested folders got built on the Figma blog

- Shape it yourself with granular control over spacing, type, and layout. Your edits stack in the chat panel, so you can review each one before you apply it.
- Point to what you mean with annotations—mark a spot and describe intent that's easier to say than to click, like "make this section feel calmer," and the agent makes the change right there.
- See it across screen sizes by switching device frames as you edit, so your design holds up everywhere.
- Reach the panel faster from the updated toolbar—
Edit
and
Annotate to the agent
are right where you start.
Read more about how the new properties panel and annotations bring a more direct way to build in Figma Make.
Learn more in the help center.

Design closer to CSS with the updated auto layout option
New release

Design
Copy link
Small differences between how auto layout and CSS handle layout meant developers had to add workarounds at handoff to make the built version match the canvas. This update closes those gaps.
Existing frames stay on the legacy version unless you choose to update. New frames get the updated version automatically. You can switch back to the legacy version until January 2027.
Learn more in the help center

When you bring code-backed screens onto the Figma canvas, colors, type, and spacing now bind to most of the variables already in your file instead of landing as hardcoded values. You'll see this when you:
Copy a Make preview
onto the canvas as design layers
Generate a design from code through
the Figma MCP server
Capture your live web page as editable layers with
the Chrome extension
More frames also come in with auto layout, so edits resize and reflow instead of needing manual cleanup. Together, this means you can bring coded or legacy screens back into Figma and spend your time refining the work, not rebuilding it.

GPT-5.6, OpenAI's latest and most capable model, is now available in Figma Make. To get started, open the model picker in the Figma Make chatbox and choose GPT-5.6. The model is available on all plans.
To see early results from our testing, read our
blog post
to learn more.
